title: Putting Statements in Standard Form
short: Turn verbs into "are" plus a class, singular statements into "All S are P", and words like "every", "none" and "a few" into the four quantifiers.
trouble: Learners write "All S are not P" for "No S are P". "All that glitters is not gold" means "Some things that glitter are not gold", an O proposition.

blocks.html: Everyday speech rarely uses the exact words of the four forms. Before you can test reasoning, you rewrite each statement in standard form. The meaning must stay the same; only the wording changes.

head: Everyday wording
Standard form
rows: All dogs are barkers (animals that bark).
None of the guests left early.
No guests are people who left early.
Not every runner is a swimmer.
All people identical to Maya are hikers.
All that glitters is not gold.
Some things that glitter are not gold things.

blocks.html: Three steps: (1) make the verb "are" plus a class ("bark" → "are barkers"); (2) choose the quantifier from the meaning: all, none, at least one, or at least one not; (3) write it as All/No/Some S are (not) P. "Many" and "most" become "some". A statement about one named thing becomes a universal about a one-member class.

Standard form has only four quantifiers, so every everyday quantifier must map to the one that keeps what it guarantees. "Most" guarantees at least one, so it becomes "some" (we lose information, but we never add any). A singular statement such as "Maya is a hiker" says something about every member of a class with exactly one member, so it acts as a universal: "All people identical to Maya are hikers."

blocks.name: lg-sort

cards.text: Every golfer is an early riser.

cards.why: "Most" keeps only "at least one": Some golfers are walkers.
No people identical to Leo are golfers.

blocks.cap: Sort each everyday statement by the form it becomes.

blocks.title: A verb and a hidden quantifier
blocks.q: Put "Some skaters dance" in standard form.
steps: Turn the verb into "are" plus a class: those who dance are dancers.

blocks.title: Not every
blocks.q: Put "Not every hiker is a poet" in standard form.
steps: "Not every hiker is a poet" says that at least one hiker is not a poet.
That is the particular negative form, O.

blocks.html: Writing "All S are not P" for "No S are P". "All S are not P" is ambiguous: "All that glitters is not gold" means that not all that glitters is gold, an O statement. Never use "All … are not" in standard form: write "No S are P" for E and "Some S are not P" for O.

sources.name: Patrick J. Hurley, A Concise Introduction to Logic, 4.7 Translating Ordinary Language Statements into Categorical Form
